title: Normalized Ricci flow preserves partial evenness and the first-odd-trace volume-renormalizability condition for smooth asymptotically hyperbolic metrics in even dimension at least four
author: Eric Bahuaud; Rafe Mazzeo; Eric Woolgar

difficulty_reason: The parity condition is imposed in a special boundary coordinate that ceases to be special under Ricci flow, so invariance cannot follow from a formal symmetry of a fixed normal form. The proof tracks all normal, mixed and tangential parity-breaking jets using explicit compactified Ricci formulas and proves a closed evolution system for the renormalizability trace. It then controls the changing defining function to recover the intrinsic boundary condition for every time of the existing flow.

proof_review.note: The complete Theorem1.1 proof in Sections3–4, the defining-function parity context in Section2 and all essential AppendixA coefficient computations were read. The authors fix the original special defining function while the metric evolves, derive coupled homogeneous evolution equations for the first parity-breaking normal/tangential coefficients, control mixed components by the supplied Christoffel/Ricci formulas, and then evolve the first odd trace coefficient. They finally translate back to the time-dependent special defining function to prove its trace still vanishes. Existing existence/uniqueness and conformal compactness of the normalized flow are credited prior background; Proposition2.5 is expressly a recalled Graham/Guillarmou result, so its sketch is not a missing new core. No renormalized-volume variation neighbour is counted.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Exactly Theorem1.1 restricted to n=2m>=4. M is the interior of a smooth compact n-manifold with boundary; g^0 is smoothly conformally compact and asymptotically hyperbolic. In Graham–Lee normal form g^0=x^-2(dx^2+h(x)), partial evenness means no odd h coefficients through order n-3. For the normalized flow partial_t g=-2(Rc(g)+(n-1)g) with initial g^0 on its maximal interval [0,T_0), partial evenness persists. If additionally tr_{h_0} h_{n-1}=0 initially, this volume-renormalizability condition also persists for the special defining function of g(t). Smooth existence, uniqueness and continued conformal compactness are the stated background flow assumptions/results; no global existence or convergence, Einstein assumption, or separate volume-variation claim is asserted.
original_metadata.editorial_warning: The evolving metric is computed in the initially fixed defining function and only later converted to its time-dependent special defining function; both parts of that proof are included. Proposition2.5 is a recalled prior Graham/Guillarmou parity result and labels its presentation a sketch; the new evolution and trace-preservation proof is supplied in full. The packet does not broaden this theorem to global-time existence.
